comments: 8d484868: ;Call the DE subroutine to set up the variables for editing

bb950e4c: ;DIE,DIC,DP,DL,DIEL,DU are standard FileMan variables.
;DG,DE,DB are local variables to hold extracted data
0fc1219f: ;If there is a date/time stamp in the 0 node, extract and save it in DE(1)
ee0f42f8: ;Clean up %Z and return
6e43d4b7: ;Write the prompt from DLB
070c3627: ;Return to caller
c064b6ca: ;Output the data in Y, wrapping at 45 characters if necessary

24a83c32: ;If the data value is longer than 19 characters and
;the input variable DV does not have I (Inquiry) or K (Key)'ed flags,
;branch to the reader code in RW^DIR2 to handle scrolling

77675e1b: ;If DV has the I (Inquiry) flag and DE(DQ) exists (is undefined),
;set X to null and output the '(No Editing)' message.
;This indicates the value cannot be edited.

6f628945: ;Read the edited value into X, timing out after DTIME
;If timeout, set DTOUT=1 and X=@ and beep the terminal
1f59404d: ;Return to caller
be728a66: Initialize data quality subscript and increment
27854c34: Branch to routine indicated by incremented data quality subscript
bab2679c: If data exists for this data quality code, branch. Otherwise write message and ask reader input
2d6446b3: If reader doesn't enter anything and data is not required, go to A. Or if data entered when not allowed, go to appropriate label based on DINUM value
833a22ce: If reader enters '?' go to question/help section, if '^' is entered execute D code and branch to ^DIE17
6534e9bc: If reader enters '@' execute D code and branch to Z^DIE2
4292d75f: If reader enters space and variable is set, show saved value from DISV unless variable indicates value should not be displayed

dff32ccf: If data is allowed, branch based on DV value. If variable set calling code from DD(DP,DIFLD,12.1) then execute it and set Y to reader entered value processed through any INPUT transforms defined in DIC("S")
80fe24c6: Loop through ';' piece to find first match to the reader entered value, calling any INPUT transforms if defined
fb5d004e: Display any remaining text after the match was found and set X to the matched value
8192cc5a: ; If it fails, quit the editing session.
7be99933: ; If number, check if precision is too long and remove excessive precision.
7188fdde: ; If number has comma (,) and file doesn't allow values with comma, remove comma and trailing zeros, and handle floating point numbers.
c9e89f58: ; Execute X cross-reference and clear temporary variables.
bd6e85b6: ; Store edited data in ^UTILITY global if requested, and quit or continue editing.
009383df: If the DATA dictionary number DQ is defined in ^DD(DQ,0) go to the tag 'Z^DIE17'
75df8305: If the data dictionary number is not defined, set the error value X to '?BAD'
5313d5d0: Go to the tag 'QQ^DIEQ' to process the input value, passing the error value X and the DIFLD variable. Then go to the label 'B'.
6b8ab585: Set the DIFLD variable to D and DQ(DQ) to the data dictionary definition piece from ^DD(DQ,0) in the format: DLB_U_DV_U_DU_U_DW_U_'X'DQ text
942131c0: If DE(DQ) is not defined, call the O^DIE tag. If X='@' go to the RD tag, if DV does not contain 'R' and X='@' go to the A tag, else if X='@' set X=Y and go to the N tag.
d56bf501: Set DG=DV, Y=DE(DQ), X=DU. If DQ(DQ,2) is defined, execute the code in DQ(DQ,2). Then go to the RP tag.

f069e59b: If DG contains 'P' and the global root ^X exists, set X to the 2nd piece of the 0 node. If the 'Y' subfile does not exist, go to RP. Else, set Y to the value in the 0 node, X to the 3rd piece of the DD field definition, and DG to the 2nd piece of the 0 node. Then go back to the R tag.

f07bdb6f: If DG contains 'V', Y is numeric, the 2nd piece of Y contains '(', and the global root pointed to by U_2nd piece of Y exists, set X to the 2nd piece of the 0 node. If the 'Y' subfile does not exist, go to RP. Else, set Y to the value in the 0 node. If the DD field definition exists, set DG to the 2nd piece and X to the 3rd piece, then go to the R tag.
5a6c8faa: If DG contains 'D', execute the ^DD('DD') routine. If DG contains 'S', set Y to the piece after the ';Y:' piece in X, if it exists.
560da793: ;Read entry; if not VARIABLE-TYPE, if DATA COMMAND less than 2, goto NODE.
c314035d: ;If INPUT TRANSFORM doesn't contain 'I' or '#', goto READ.
f1d16f7c: ;Execute INPUT TRANSFORM, goto READ if X is defined, else goto PROCESSED.
7cced0fd: ;Quit.
a30bfa90: ;Initialize variables.
780cd545: ;Set DIEDIT parameters.
a88fe71e: ;Goto ENTRY READER.
eef01f63: ;Read date, convert to internal format.
e6d44edf: ;Quit.

5427ea7d: ;If double-valued field, call FIELD HELP, Execute TRANS HELP, set Y to up-arrow, set DATA QUALITY=2, goto X2. If Y is defined and not up-arrow, set X=Y, set DIC(0)='F', set DATA WORD=DATA QUALITY, goto OUTPUT TRANSFORM.
cfd9cccd: Clear the field indicating the date transcribed if the date transcribed is being deleted.
4fba6844: Exit.
78ebe037: If data exists, call FileMan hooks and execute input transforms for field 3 (DATE TRANSCRIBED). Store the user's response in Y. Pass control to DIE17^DIE17 based on conditions.
4db3333b: If the date transcribed is before the date dictated, display an error message and set internal entry for re-editing.
3f31ed81: Exit.
e1195c90: If data exists, call FileMan hooks and execute input transforms for field 4 (STATUS). Store the user's response in Y. Pass control to DIE17^DIE17 based on conditions.
6a28cdae: If the STATUS field is left blank, set it to 'TRANSCRIBED' and set internal entry for re-editing.
f46425ab: Exit.
0b174af3: If data exists, call FileMan hooks. Pass control to routine DGJXE14.
